summary: Kuntala Bhattacharya works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Supervised by Prabal Kumar Sen for an MA and by Amita Chatterjee and Shyamapada Misra for a PhD at Jadavpur University, she held an attested post at Rabindra Bharati University in 2009.
Kunzang Namgyal was a scholar who studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrõl Lodrö Thaye.

Kunzang Pelden studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He taught prominent students, including Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, and Shechen Gyaltsab.

id: P:Kunzig Shamar Rinpoche Mipham Chokyi Lodro
summary: Kunzig Shamar Rinpoche Mipham Chokyi Lodro (1952–2014) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers, including the 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Kalu Rinpoche (in 1973).

Kuo-Pin Chuang earned a PhD from National Chung Hsing University, specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held postdoctoral posts at National Taiwan University (2019–2022) and the University of Edinburgh (2022), later becoming a professor at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.

Kurt A. Behrendt (born 1964) works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After earning his PhD from UCLA (~1991–1997), he served at the Metropolitan Museum of Art as Assistant Curator (~2006) and Associate Curator of South Asian Art (~2014).
Kurt Andrew Johnson is a scholar in Indology. He earned his PhD from the University of York by 2010, studying under doctoral supervisor Jane Moody.
Kurt Bruno Otto Fischer (1892–1942) worked in Buddhist studies. A pupil of Paul Dahlke from ~1920 to 1928, he succeeded Dahlke in 1928 and led Das Buddhistische Haus from ~1928 to 1930.

Kurt Friedrich Leidecker (1902–1991) worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, earning a BA from Oberlin (~1921–1924) and a PhD from Chicago (~1924–1927). He taught at Rensselaer, Lehigh, and Mary Washington, and directed the Thomas Jefferson Institute in 1974.

Kurt Huber (1893–1943) was a philosopher who studied at Eberhard-Ludwigs-Gymnasium and earned his PhD at the University of Munich (~1913–1917). He later taught Hans Hartog and held professor positions at the University of Munich in 1926 and 1938.
Kurt Hutten (1901–1979) was a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Tübingen (~1920–1930) under the supervision of Jakob Wilhelm Hauer.

Kurt Klemm (1852–1908) studied Indology and linguistics at Humboldt University and the University of Leipzig (~1888–1894, PhD). His teachers included Albrecht Weber, Karl Friedrich Geldner, Johannes Schmidt, Ernst Windisch, and Karl Brugmann.
Kurt Quecke (1924–1975) was a scholar in Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Marburg by 1947 under the supervision of Johannes Nobel.
Kurt Schmidt (1879–1975) was active in Buddhist studies. He completed a Dr. iuris at the University of Rostock (~1900–1901) and founded the Buddhistische Arbeitsgemeinschaft in 1946.

Linguist Kurt Stegmann von Pritzwald (1901–1962) studied at Giessen, Munich, and Jena (PhD under Albert Debrunner). He taught at Jena, Kiel, Rostock, and Marburg, where he became apl. Professor of general and comparative linguistics in 1945.

Kurt Tropper works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a doctoral degree from the University of Vienna in 2001 under Ernst Steinkellner, and studied with Michael Torsten Much and Tashi Geisler. He held posts at Vienna and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

Kurt Wulff (1881–1939) was a scholar in linguistics and sinology educated at Copenhagen, Oxford, and Leipzig. He worked at the Thesaurus Linguae Latinae and the Royal Danish Library, before serving as a lecturer and docent at the University of Copenhagen.

Kurt von Kamptz (1897–1941) was an Indology scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg (~1924–1929) under Walther Schubring. He later worked as a librarian at Wehrkreisbücherei IV in Dresden.

Kurtis R. Schaeffer is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After degrees from Lewis & Clark, Evergreen, Washington, and Harvard (PhD ~2000), he held faculty appointments at the University of Alabama (2000–2004) and the University of Virginia (from 2005).
Kurunegoda Piyatissa (1928–2008) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a post at the New York Buddhist Vihara, where he was attested as head in 1998.
